01 · What the room needs

A service is five jobs, in signal order.

Light the platform. Cameras see what the room sees, only less forgiving. One daylight key from the back of the room lifts faces out of the stage wash, so the stream doesn’t look darker than the service.

Capture. PTZ cameras sit on a wall or a shelf, out of the congregation’s sightline, and one person moves them from the booth. Zoom is what matters most: the distance from camera to pulpit decides whether you get a close-up or only a medium shot.

Mic the pulpit and the worship team. Wireless handhelds for the pastor and the worship leader; headsets when hands need to be free. Every voice that reaches the room should also reach the stream.

Mix. The room mix and the stream mix are not the same mix. A digital mixer that records every channel lets you fix the stream later and rehearse with last Sunday’s tracks.

Switch and stream. A switcher cuts between cameras and slides and sends one program to YouTube or your site. Keep it simple enough that the volunteer on duty this week can run it.

Size every job to the room, not to the brochure. The distance from the booth to the pulpit decides the camera’s zoom; the number of voices on a busy Sunday decides the mixer; how often the team changes decides how simple the switcher has to be. That is why the chain below is a starting point, and why a specialist asks about the room before quoting it.

Church livestream questions.

What churches ask before they buy.

What equipment do you need to livestream a church service?

Light on the platform, at least one camera, microphones for the pulpit and the worship team, a mixer, and a switcher that sends the program to your stream. The church chain on this page is one listing per job: $4,859.99 at listed prices.

How many cameras does a church livestream need?

One camera can carry a service. Two let one hold the wide while the other follows the speaker, which is the one-operator setup here. Three on the network, with a joystick for presets, is the larger setup.

Can volunteers run it?

The one-operator setup is built for one person in the booth: two PTZ cameras on presets, a four-input switcher with buttons for each camera, and headphones to hear the stream mix.

How far can a PTZ camera be from the pulpit?

It depends on the zoom. A 12× camera frames a head-and-shoulders close-up out to about 19 ft; a 24× camera to about 34 ft. The PTZ distance calculator works it out for any camera and distance.

Can a church buy without sales tax?

Yes. Religious institutions and resellers with an approved exemption certificate do not pay sales tax. Attach the certificate at checkout or send it with a quote.

Who installs it?

i9TV, i9’s integration company, installs, configures and trains your team in Florida and Brazil; elsewhere in Latin America under an installation, configuration and training contract. A support plan (SLA) is quoted with the project.
